title: Thomae's Function is Riemann Integrable (integral 0)
description: Shows Thomae's (popcorn) function is integrable on [0,1] with integral 0. Rather than the textbook Lebesgue criterion (which Mathlib does not expose as a ready lemma, and Mathlib has no first-class RiemannIntegrable predicate — its intervalIntegral IS the Bochner/Lebesgue integral), the proof takes the direct route: thomae =ᵐ[volume] 0, because thomae x ≠ 0 only on the rationals, a countable (hence null) set. From a.e.-equality to 0 it derives Integrable thomae volume and ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, thomae x = 0. Builds on the parent entry's thomae_irrational. 5 theorems, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Thomae's function (the 'popcorn' or 'ruler' function) is 1/q for x = p/q in lowest terms and 0 for irrational x. It is the classic example of a function continuous at every irrational and discontinuous at every rational, yet Riemann integrable with integral 0 — a standard counterpoint to the Dirichlet function (which is nowhere continuous and not Riemann integrable). The textbook proof invokes the Lebesgue criterion: a bounded function is Riemann integrable iff its set of discontinuities is null. In Lean/Mathlib the situation is different: there is no first-class RiemannIntegrable predicate, and intervalIntegral is already the Bochner/Lebesgue integral, so the right formal target is the value of that integral.
overview.problemStatement: Show that Thomae's function $t$ is integrable on $[0,1]$ and $\int_0^1 t = 0$, where $t(p/q) = 1/q$ for $p/q$ in lowest terms and $t(x) = 0$ for irrational $x$.
overview.text: Because $t(x) \neq 0$ only when $x$ is rational, the support of $t$ is contained in the countable set $\{(\uparrow q) : q \in \mathbb{Q}\}$, which has Lebesgue measure zero. Hence $t =ᵐ 0$, so $t$ is integrable (it agrees a.e. with the zero function) and its integral equals that of $0$, namely $0$.
overview.proofStrategy: Five steps. (1) thomae_support_subset_rat: if t(x) ≠ 0 then x is rational — proved by by_contra, since Irrational x is definitionally x ∉ range((↑):ℚ→ℝ), feeding the parent's thomae_irrational. (2) thomae_support_null: the support is null, by measure_mono_null into the countable range (Set.countable_range + Set.Countable.measure_zero under NoAtoms volume). (3) thomae_ae_eq_zero: t =ᵐ 0, via ae_iff reducing to the support-null statement. (4) thomae_integrable: (integrable_zero ℝ ℝ volume).congr of the a.e.-equality. (5) thomae_intervalIntegral_zero: intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae rewrites the integral to that of 0, closed by intervalIntegral.integral_zero.
keyInsights: The Lebesgue criterion is the wrong Lean target. Mathlib exposes neither a RiemannIntegrable predicate nor the 'integrable ⇔ continuous a.e.' criterion as a usable lemma; since intervalIntegral is the Lebesgue integral, the natural goal is the integral's value, reached directly via a.e.-equality.

Only thomae_irrational is needed, not the continuity theorems. The integrability follows purely from 'support ⊆ ℚ ⟹ a.e. zero'; the parent's continuity-at-irrationals / discontinuity-at-rationals results are irrelevant to this route (they would only be needed for the Lebesgue-criterion phrasing).
Countability does all the measure-theoretic work. range((↑):ℚ→ℝ) is countable because ℚ is, and ℝ has no atoms, so the support is null — no fine structure of 1/q values is used.

Irrational is definitionally a non-membership. Irrational x unfolds to x ∉ Set.range ((↑):ℚ→ℝ), so the by_contra hypothesis in step 1 is exactly what thomae_irrational consumes, with no coercion bookkeeping.

Integrability and integral value are both a.e.-class facts. Once thomae =ᵐ 0 is established, integrability transfers by Integrable.congr and the integral value by intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae — both because the Bochner integral and the Integrable predicate are invariant under a.e.-equality. The single reduction to the zero function therefore settles both the qualitative (integrable) and quantitative (= 0) claims at once.

conclusion.summary: Thomae's function is integrable on [0,1] with integral 0, proved via the a.e.-zero route (support ⊆ countable ℚ ⟹ null) rather than the Mathlib-absent Lebesgue criterion. 5 theorems, 0 axioms, 68 lines. Build-pending (deferred to deployer build-gate).
conclusion.implications: Provides the integrability companion to the parent's continuity analysis of Thomae's function, and documents the idiom for 'Riemann integrable with integral v' in a library where intervalIntegral is the Lebesgue integral and no Lebesgue criterion is available: localize the support, show it is null, pass to a.e.-equality. The same pattern applies to any function supported on a countable (or null) set.

sections.title: Support Localization and Nullity
sections.summary: thomae_support_subset_rat localizes the nonzero set inside range((↑):ℚ→ℝ) via by_contra + thomae_irrational; thomae_support_null concludes the support is null by measure_mono_null into the countable range under NoAtoms volume.

sections.title: Almost-Everywhere Zero
sections.summary: thomae_ae_eq_zero rewrites the a.e.-equality goal via ae_iff to the support-null statement (after simp [Pi.zero_apply, ne_eq]).

sections.title: Integrability by Transfer
sections.summary: thomae_integrable transfers integrability from the zero function by Integrable.congr applied to thomae_ae_eq_zero.symm — integrability is an a.e.-class property, so no boundedness or continuity is invoked.

sections.title: The Integral Value is Zero
sections.summary: thomae_intervalIntegral_zero rewrites ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, thomae x to the integral of 0 via intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae (using thomae_ae_eq_zero.mono to restrict the a.e.-equality to [0,1]) and closes with intervalIntegral.integral_zero.
